title: Transient bioelectric and serotonergic perturbation induces a melanoma-like phenotype

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Transient bioelectric and serotonergic perturbation induces a melanoma-like phenotype

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Transient perturbation of bioelectrical and serotonergic signalling among cells can induce a melanoma-like phenotype in the absence of carcinogens, oncogenes or DNA damage.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Cancer and the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: (b) transient perturbation of bioelectrical and serotonergic signaling among cells can induce a melanoma‐like phenotype in the absence of carcinogens, oncogenes, or DNA damage [176, 177, 178]

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Cancer and the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos and their melanocytes (author's lab's prior work, refs [176–178])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The perturbations, negative conditions and phenotype components are explicit and discriminating. The reported experiments can resolve the restricted Xenopus claim, but public raw-data completeness and the strength of the no-DNA-damage condition are uncertain.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare melanocyte proliferation, migration, vascular or brain invasion and morphology after transient bioelectric or serotonergic perturbation with vehicle, oncogene and DNA-damage controls. A melanoma-like suite in genetically normal, damage-negative animals supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw animal-level data may remain in paper supplements.

Excluding all DNA damage requires direct assays.

Melanoma-like is a phenotype analogy rather than a tumour diagnosis.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.95
discriminating power: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The experiment is operational: a short physiological perturbation, explicit negative controls for the usual carcinogenic causes, and a pigment-cell phenotype. Those measurements were reported by the originating studies and were not deposited as analyzable counts or images. Human tumor archives do not contain the transient-perturbation design, so the claim needs data that are not yet public.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Transiently perturb bioelectric and serotonergic signalling in Xenopus melanocytes, then score a pre-specified melanoma-like phenotype against controls that lack carcinogen, oncogene, and detectable DNA damage. Induction by the transient perturbation alone would support the claim; dependence on DNA damage or an oncogene would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Melanoma-like needs a fixed histological criterion to avoid circular scoring.

Melanoma genomics resources are human tumors, not this embryonic conversion assay.

Phenotype counts, serotonin manipulations, and DNA-damage controls are not in a public dataset.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.55
data existence: 0.25
data adequacy: 0.25
